priced_in_summary: WATCH on the COMPOUNDER clock. This is a real, evidenced, fresh-context-audited exposure (one of four dominant US environmental and sustainability consulting firms, an ENR #1-in-18-categories leader including Data Centers) sitting on a company with clean-to-strong mechanical earnings quality (Piotroski 7 STRONG, Beneish CLEAN, Altman SAFE) and confirmed, filed operating momentum (record $28.9 billion backlog, three consecutive guidance raises). But two things stop this at WATCH rather than INVESTABLE. First, the specific occurrence this chain names, mandated environmental-impact studies triggered by permitting freezes, has no separate disclosure anywhere on disk; an investor buying J for this reason is really buying the much larger, already-well-covered AI-and-data-center-capex story and hoping the narrower permitting thread is a real incremental driver inside it. FY2025's own operating cash flow fell 34.9% even as operating income rose 24.7%, a divergence this run's single fetched document does not decompose, and until the FY2025 10-K (not fetched this run) is read, this dive cannot say with confidence whether the market is over-asking or the filed base year is simply understated. Not INVESTABLE: no entry basis this dive can defend with confidence exists at today's price given that fragility. Not TOO_LATE: the priced-in decomposition does not show a story running purely on multiple expansion; the rally since the 2026-05-13 low (+36.32%) tracks filed beat-and-raise fundamentals (backlog, guidance) rather than a re-rating with no fundamental confirmation, and the stock sits 11.07% below its 52-week high, not at a fresh one.

Layered on top, Engineering News-Record ranked Jacobs #1 in 18 categories including Data Centers in 2026, 'up 6 y/y', and record backlog reached $28.9 billion, up 27.3% year-over-year with a trailing book-to-bill of 1.4x, both verbatim from the Q3 FY2026 8-K (accession 0001628280-26-052563).

The mechanical earnings-quality battery is clean-to-strong and the balance sheet has room: Piotroski 7 of 9 (STRONG, 9/9 inputs), Beneish M-score -2.582 against a -1.78 review threshold (CLEAN, 12/12 inputs), Altman Z 3.05 (SAFE), accruals of -3.45% of average assets (net income $289.336M against operating cash flow $686.704M, average total assets $11,505.77M FY2024-2025), a conservative direction, and net debt to EBITDA of 2.545x even after closing the ~$1.6 billion PA Consulting Transaction (2026-03-20) and returning $614 million to shareholders via buybacks year-to-date, with the CFO stating verbatim that Q3 free cash flow 'helped reduce our net leverage to below our year-end target.'

bear: The specific occurrence this chain names, mandated multi-year environmental-impact studies triggered by state and municipal data-center permitting freezes, is not separately disclosed or quantified anywhere on disk: every filed and press figure this run found describes Jacobs' broad AI-and-data-center-capex exposure (design, EPCM such as the Hut 8 Texas contract, cooling, power) as one blended number, so an investor buying J for this occurrence specifically is buying a much larger, already-well-covered AI-infrastructure story and hoping the narrower permitting-consultancy thread is a real incremental driver inside it, per the profile's own selection_basis.evidence_confidence.known_weaknesses.

(3) State and municipal permitting freezes of the New York Executive Order 62 type proliferate faster and more severely than this dive's base case assumed, generating incremental (not merely relabeled) mandated-study demand that shows up first in the already-growing $28.9B backlog and 1.4x book-to-bill well before the FY2026 year-end print this dive set as its own leading indicator, so the stock moves through and past the modeled would-buy zone before the 2026-11-30 review date gives this file a chance to re-price it. Because this dive can articulate genuine, evidence-grounded reasons the market could turn out to have been right (reason 1 in particular is not hypothetical, it is this dive's own unresolved conversion-ratio finding read the other way), the pre-mortem does not force a downgrade; the verdict was already WATCH, the floor method section 7 sets for exactly this situation.
red_team.surviving_bear_case: Buying J today for the data-center-moratoria occurrence specifically means buying a much larger, already well-covered AI-and-data-center-capex story and hoping a narrower permitting-consultancy thread, nowhere separately disclosed by the company and shared with at least three named peers (AECOM, WSP, Tetra Tech) holding the same market-share basket, is a real incremental driver rather than a relabeling of demand Jacobs would have captured anyway; this red team's independent capture-score read (48, differentiated but competed) argues competitive bidding among those peers can let data-center customers capture more of any incremental-study surplus than a clean, moated re-rating thesis would need. Layered on that is this dive's own central valuation finding, now independently rebuilt and confirmed rather than merely asserted: the market's roughly 21% five-year FCF-CAGR ask is real against this dive's 8.5%-revenue/8.0%-margin build only at the exact intersection of the filed 9% discount rate, FY2025's base cash flow, and that year's unusually low 70.3% operating-income-to-FCF conversion, and it collapses toward the file's own no-gap tolerance under any single one of four individually plausible alternative conventions (a longer horizon, a four-year-average cash-flow base, a discount rate at or below 8%, or a four-year-average conversion ratio, the last of which alone implies a fair price near $135, just 7.5% below today's close). That fragility, not a clean over- or under-valuation call, is why this stays WATCH rather than becoming INVESTABLE (no defensible single entry basis at today's price) or TOO_LATE (the rally tracks filed backlog and guidance beats, not a bare re-rating): the honest position is that the market and this dive disagree about which of Jacobs' recent numbers is the anomaly, FY2025's cash conversion or the market's own extrapolation of one strong quarter, and until the un-fetched FY2025 10-K settles that question, no price on today's board can be defended with confidence as a buy. Separately, this red team confirms J's would_buy_zone repeats a corpus-wide construction defect the same-day WST and CMI red teams already escalated: the zone is solved against this dive's own base/stretch case for the revenue-growth row (8.5-9.5%, at or above the 65th-percentile 'mine' estimate), not against a separately built bear case, so method section 7's own bear-case-survival requirement for a would-buy zone is not demonstrated here any more than it was on VRT, MYRG, WST or CMI; this is named and escalated to Ron rather than resolved by this run inventing its own bear-case zone.

would_buy_stress: This zone is drawn at FY2025's own cash-conversion ratio (70.3% of operating income), which expectations_gap.rows[net_gap_direction] already found is the single largest lever in this whole dive. A reader who believes FY2025's low conversion is the anomaly, not the average FY2022-2025 conversion, should treat $135.28 as the more relevant number and this zone as a conservative floor rather than a realistic near-term entry level. This dive does not pick between the two readings; data_gaps names the FY2025 10-K, not fetched this run, as the document that would resolve which conversion ratio is the anomaly.
